fixed: CRITICAL: sentiment label order was hardcoded as [negative, neutral, positive] while dicta-il/dictabert-sentiment ships id2label {0: Positive, 1: Negative, 2: Neutral}. Every emitted label was wrong at every index, so a frustration spike read as a satisfaction spike. Now reads model.config.id2label and recommends the pipeline() entry point.

Dashboard intent_accuracy was computed as share of predictions above a confidence threshold and rendered under the Hebrew label for accuracy. Split into high_confidence_rate (always populated) and intent_accuracy (None unless labelled data exists, rendered n/a otherwise).
Drop-off-by-intent excluded fallback, emptying the report for the most common real drop-off pattern and contradicting the skill's own spec. Fallback is now kept.

deferred.title: LLM and RAG bot observability, evals and cost
deferred.why_deferred: It is an addition, not a correction, and this cycle was scoped to correctness only.
deferred.detail: The skill is an NLU-era artifact. Everything it measures (intent accuracy, confusion matrices, fallback rate, matched_intent) is a metric family that does not exist on an LLM bot, and the skill half-acknowledges this in its own CALM notes without acting on it. A 2026 Hebrew support chatbot is almost certainly an LLM/RAG agent. Missing, in priority order: (1) Groundedness and hallucination rate, the top quality metric for a Hebrew RAG support bot and the one with real legal exposure when the bot states a wrong price or statutory entitlement; use the RAG-triad decomposition of Context Relevance, Answer Relevance, Groundedness. (2) LLM-as-judge eval loops in Hebrew against a labelled golden set, replacing the current advice to hand-label 100-200 conversations per week. (3) Tracing via Langfuse, LangSmith or Arize Phoenix, plus the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (CNCF-backed, adopted by Google Cloud, AWS, Azure and Datadog, still largely experimental as of March 2026, scope now covering agent orchestration, MCP tool calling, content capture and quality evaluation). (4) Cost per conversation: token spend per resolved session is what gets an LLM bot funded or killed, and the dashboard currently tracks response-time percentiles but not one cost field while a whole section covers WhatsApp per-message cost. (5) Tool-call success rate, and TTFT versus total latency, since streaming makes avg_response_time_ms close to meaningless. Implementation shape: a new step between Steps 5 and 6, plus tokens_in / tokens_out / model / tool_calls added to the conversation log schema in Step 1. If scope must be traded, cut depth from Step 5's confusion-matrix machinery, which is dead weight on a CALM or LLM bot by the skill's own admission.

watch_items.detail: Meta's pricing page currently states that utility templates sent within an open customer service window are free, and links a pricing explainer that 'reflects updates launching October 1, 2026' without stating the content. Several BSP guides claim in-window utility templates start being charged on 2026-10-01. Not written into the skill as fact. Re-check the Meta page after 2026-10-01.

The Botpress Hebrew RTL gap cited in the platform table rests on a Discord thread that returns HTTP 429 to automated fetches. Could not re-confirm the gap is still open. Re-check in a browser next cycle.
Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026. The skill now requires 3.11+.

lessons: Never trust a label list that looks alphabetical or looks like a natural ordering. Model label order is metadata; read config.id2label. This defect survived two prior reviews because the literal ['negative','neutral','positive'] reads as obviously correct.
A metric can be defined correctly in the glossary, computed correctly in one step, and silently redefined in another. Grep for every field name across all steps, not just the step that introduces it.

Execution finds defects that reading does not. Running the bundled script on a fixture whose only abandoned-session intent was 'fallback' is what exposed the missing drop-off block; reading the function did not.
Silent exception handlers are worse than crashes in an analytics tool. Two bare except:pass handlers turned a Python-version incompatibility into empty output with no error.

Check that a cited source actually contains the claim. The Statsig page cited for the OpenAI acquisition does not mention it anywhere, and the DLA Piper page cited for IM-app coverage says only 'automated dialing, fax or text messages'. Both had been carried as high confidence.
Benchmark tables attract an authority they have not earned. Five thresholds were labelled 'Israeli market' with a single generic global source behind one unrelated row.
